text: Social media has become part of daily life for billions of people. Platforms such as Instagram and TikTok allow users to share photos, videos, and opinions instantly, and they help people connect with friends and family around the world. However, many researchers believe these platforms can also influence users in negative ways. Because content is designed to be addictive, some people spend hours scrolling every day, which can lead to addiction. When users constantly compare their lives to the perfect images posted by an influencer, it can damage their self-esteem and increase anxiety. Although social media helps people stay in touch, it can also isolate them from real face-to-face relationships. A single post can go viral overnight, reaching millions of people, but this attention is not always positive; a careless comment can follow someone for years. In addition, many users worry about their privacy, as companies collect personal data from every click. As a result, schools and organizations are raising awareness about the risks of following the latest trend without thinking. Learning to engage with social media in a balanced way is essential for both mental health and safety.
